title: Longest Ones After One Deletion
statement: You get an array bits of 0s and 1s. You must delete exactly one element. After the deletion, return the length of the longest contiguous run made only of 1s. Return 0 if there is none.

examples.why: Delete the 0 at index 2 to join 1, 1 with 1, 1, 1.
The deletion is compulsory, so one 1 has to go.
Two zeros in a row cannot both be removed, so the 1 on the left never joins the pair on the right.

hints: Deleting one element merges the runs of 1s on both sides of it. What does a window that may contain at most one 0 look like?
Slide a window that holds at most one 0. Its length minus one is a candidate answer, because one element of it gets deleted.
Grow the right end; when the window holds two zeros, move the left end past the first of them. Track the best right − left.

explain.intuition:
After deleting one element, a run of 1s is just a stretch of the original array that contains at most one 0 (the one you deleted), minus one element. If the stretch has no 0 at all, you still delete one of its 1s, so the "minus one" holds there too, which is exactly why [1, 1, 1] gives 2.

So the task is: find the longest window with at most one 0, and subtract 1. That is the standard sliding window: extend the right end, and whenever a second 0 enters, move the left end past the older 0. Like a debounce that keeps only the latest event, the window remembers only the most recent zero.
steps: While zeros > 1, if bits[left] is 0 decrement zeros; then move left right.
Update best = max(best, right − left). That is the window length minus the deleted element.
pitfalls: Returning the full length when there are no zeros. Something must still be deleted (example 2).
Merging runs across two or more zeros. Only one element goes (example 3).
Returning the window length instead of length − 1.

solutions.title: Try every deletion
solutions.idea: Delete each position in turn and measure the longest run of 1s that remains.

solutions.title: Sliding window with at most one zero
solutions.idea: The longest window holding at most one 0, minus the one deleted element.

followups: You may delete up to k elements instead of exactly one. What changes?
Instead of deleting, you may flip one 0 into a 1. How does the answer relate to this one?
